chunks: And it is narrated from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked him about a man who said to three of his slaves, “You are free,” while he had four.
Then a man from among the people said to him, “You have freed your slaves.” He said, “Yes.”
Is the emancipation binding for all four when he spoke of them generally, or is it for the three whom he freed?
He said: “Emancipation is binding only for those whom he freed.”

key_terms.أَجْمَلَهُمْ: he referred to them in a general, non-specific way
key_terms.أَحْرَارٌ: freed persons no longer held in bondage
key_terms.عِتْقُ: the legal act and effect of emancipation
key_terms.مَمَالِيكَ: slaves owned by the man in this legal case

ai.seo_question: If someone frees only some of his slaves but later speaks generally, does emancipation apply to all of them?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about emancipation. If a man explicitly frees three slaves and later answers generally in a way that could seem to include all of them, the ruling remains limited to those he specifically emancipated. The hadith emphasizes that legal effect follows the actual act of emancipation, not a vague generalization afterward.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3443 - It is narrated from Sama'ah, who said:
I asked him about a man who said to three of his slaves, "You are free," while he actually had four slaves.

Then someone said to him: "You have freed all your slaves."
He replied: "Yes."
I asked: "Is the emancipation binding for all four because he generalized them, or is it limited to the three whom he specifically mentioned?"
Imam (as) said: "Emancipation is binding only for those he specifically freed."
